description: Internal API of the privileged HinterOS system service (hinteros-system, root). Any process of a 'hinteros' user can connect; the session daemon is an ordinary client that relays these methods to the launcher. Read-only methods need no further checks. Mutating methods need a pidfd for the peer (SO_PEERPIDFD), the caller owning seat0's active session (or root), a polkit YES for the method's action (with user interaction only for org.hinteros.system.ssh, whose default is auth_admin: polkit then asks the calling process's authentication agent for the admin password while the call waits), and are rate limited and audited in the system journal. Every params object is closed: unknown fields are invalid_params. Long work runs as a job in its own systemd unit and reports through job_* events. See hinteros-docs/design/system-api.md.

hello.summary: Version handshake. Must be the first request on a connection, within 5 seconds.

ping.summary: Liveness check. Echoes the optional nonce.

subscribe.summary: Start receiving the given events on this connection. Returns the full subscription set.

unsubscribe.summary: Stop receiving the given events on this connection. Returns the remaining subscription set.

system.info.summary: What is running: release, channel, base, locked revision, generation, hostname, dev build, SSH state and host key fingerprints. Read-only.

version.description: HinterOS release of the running generation, or 'unknown'.

channel.description: Channel /etc/hinteros follows; null without a locked channel (the dev box).

dev.description: A dev build (hinteros.dev.enable): the launcher shows a DEV badge.

host_key_fingerprints.description: SHA256 fingerprints of the SSH host keys, for checking the first connection.

settings.get.summary: The user-settable view of state.json and its revision (a hash of the file). Read-only.

apps.description: Schema-1 boxes: catalog app ids installed box-wide from the Store (state.json apps), in install order (since 0.3). Absent on schema-2 boxes (0.4: apps are per profile, see apps.list).

requirements.description: Schema-2 boxes (0.4): the box features that are on (read-only).

enabled.description: sshd runs; login is the admin account with its password.

settings.set.description: changes is a closed, typed object: each settable state.json field is a property here (bool, enum, bounded integer), never free-form. It has no properties in 0.2 (SSH, base and channel have their own methods), so any field is invalid_params with data {field, reason: unknown_field}, and an empty changes object returns job_id null. revision must equal settings.get's, else state_conflict. The service writes state.json from its own typed state, never the caller's bytes.

ssh.set.summary: Turn SSH (sshd) on or off (job). Action org.hinteros.system.ssh, which needs the admin password (auth_admin).
ssh.set.description: Login over SSH is the admin account with its password; the system repo configures sshd. polkit's default for this action is auth_admin. The service checks it with AllowUserInteraction (since 0.3): polkit asks the authentication agent registered for the calling process (the session daemon's, which shows the launcher a password prompt) and the call waits until the user answered (at most 5 minutes). Without an agent the call gets authentication_required; a cancelled or timed-out prompt also gives authentication_required, too many wrong passwords permission_denied (reason polkit). Returns job_id null if SSH already is in that state.

error.message: caller does not own the active seat0 session

generations.list.summary: System generations on disk (newest first). Read-only.

rebuild.summary: Re-apply the current /etc/hinteros (job): repair after a failed switch. Action org.hinteros.system.rebuild.

hardware.redetect.summary: Regenerate facter.json with nixos-facter and apply it (job). Action org.hinteros.system.rebuild.
hardware.redetect.description: On a schema-2 box (0.5) the admin profile's PIN is needed in admin_pin (pin_required {pin: admin} when it is missing or wrong, or when there is no admin profile yet); an admin profile without a PIN yet passes. Not needed on a schema-1 box or from root.

rollback.summary: Switch to an earlier generation (default: the one before the current), then restore /etc/hinteros from its snapshot (job). Action org.hinteros.system.rollback.
rollback.description: On a schema-2 box (0.5) the admin profile's PIN is needed in admin_pin (pin_required {pin: admin} when it is missing or wrong, or when there is no admin profile yet); an admin profile without a PIN yet passes. Not needed on a schema-1 box or from root. After the switch and the apps stage (schema 2), box features that the owners' current app envs need and the restored generation lacks are turned back on in a box stage: the apply flow on the restored configuration with requirements = what the envs need (a second, mostly cached build; a new generation). The result then lists them in features_readded; generations.list names them beforehand per generation (readds_features). If that build fails the job fails at stage box (the rollback itself stays).

update.check.summary: Look for a newer signed revision of the channel (job), or, within 60 s of the last check, return that result without a job. Action org.hinteros.system.update.check.
update.check.description: The job lists the channel branch (git ls-remote of the URL from the running generation's channel table), fetches it into a root-owned bare repo, verifies the tip's SSH signature against the allowed signers shipped in the running generation, requires it to descend from the locked revision, and reads the highest Security: <low|medium|high|critical> trailer among the new commits. The job's result is an UpdateCheckResult; failures are job_failed, update_unreachable or update_verification_failed in job_finished.error.

available.security_summary: A website could take over the browser in a profile.

update.apply.summary: Install the revision found by the last update.check (job). Action org.hinteros.system.update.apply.
update.apply.description: rev must equal the last verified check result's available.rev for the current channel and locked revision, else state_conflict. The job re-verifies it, locks the hinteros input to ?rev=<rev> (never re-fetching the branch) and runs the apply flow.

error.message: rev is not the last verified update

channel.set.description: The URL comes from the running generation's channel table, never from params. The target tip must be signed by an allowed signer. Moving from beta to stable, or to a tip that does not descend from the locked revision, needs acknowledge_downgrade: true (else needs_acknowledgement: at once for beta to stable, in job_finished.error for a non-fast-forward tip). Returns job_id null if the channel is already the current one. On a schema-2 box (0.5) the admin profile's PIN is needed in admin_pin (pin_required {pin: admin} when it is missing or wrong, or when there is no admin profile yet); an admin profile without a PIN yet passes. Not needed on a schema-1 box or from root.

error.message: switching from beta to stable is a downgrade

base.set.summary: Switch the nixpkgs base (job). Action org.hinteros.system.channel. unstable to stable needs acknowledge_downgrade: true.
base.set.description: On a schema-2 box (0.5) the admin profile's PIN is needed in admin_pin (pin_required {pin: admin} when it is missing or wrong, or when there is no admin profile yet); an admin profile without a PIN yet passes. Not needed on a schema-1 box or from root. The PIN is checked before anything else, also when the base is already the requested one.

error.message: unstable to stable is a downgrade

apps.install.description: ids (1 to 8 catalog ids) must be in the running generation's catalog index (/run/current-system/sw/share/hinteros/catalog.json, never the caller's copy) with status available; their depends are added (transitively). Ids already installed are skipped; if nothing is left the result is job_id null. A conflict between a new app and an installed or requested one is app_conflict. Every new app with vendor terms needs accepted_terms[id] equal to the catalog's terms.version, else terms_required (the box records the acceptance: id, version, time, uid and profile, in the audit log and /var/lib/hinteros/terms-accepted.json). revision must be settings.get's (state_conflict otherwise); 0.4, schema-2 boxes: the app revision from apps.list, and the apps are installed into the caller's own profile (a new generation of its Nix profile, no system rebuild unless a box feature must be turned on first: stage box). Free disk space must cover the new apps' sizeMiB plus the usual rebuild margin (insufficient_resources). The job writes state.json's apps from the service's typed state and runs the apply flow.

accepted_terms.description: App id to the terms version the user accepted (after reading the full text).

error.message: nope is not in this system's catalog

apps.remove.summary: Remove installed Store apps (job), optionally with their data. Action org.hinteros.system.apps.
apps.remove.description: ids (1 to 8) must be installed (not_found otherwise). An app that another installed app depends on cannot be removed alone (app_conflict, conflicts_with names the dependent). The job writes state.json without them and runs the apply flow. With delete_data, after a successful switch the job deletes each removed app's dataPaths (from the running generation's catalog) in every profile's home, as root without following symlinks (each path component is opened with O_NOFOLLOW relative to the home; nothing outside the home and no other filesystem is touched) and logs what it deleted. The launcher closes running apps first.

apps.list.summary: The caller's own apps (0.4, schema-2 boxes): its current app env.
apps.list.description: Read-only. The caller is resolved from its uid: a profile (or the guest). revision stands for the current app generation; pass it to apps.install/apps.remove as revision. needs_terms: ids whose vendor terms this profile has not accepted at the catalog's current version (apps that came with the starter set); the launcher shows the terms on first launch and calls apps.accept_terms. A spare account gets an empty list. Schema-1 boxes (not migrated yet): unavailable {service: profiles, reason: schema1}.

examples.name: a profile with Steam from the starter set

error.message: this box has not moved to per-profile apps yet

apps.generations.summary: The caller's app generations (0.4), newest first.
apps.generations.description: Read-only. Every generation of the caller's Nix profile of apps (the newest 3 plus the current one are kept), with the ids of its env and the system revision it was built against. apps.rollback takes one of them.

apps.rollback.summary: Switch the caller's apps back to an earlier generation (job, 0.4). Action org.hinteros.system.apps.
apps.rollback.description: generation must be one of apps.generations and not the current one (not_found otherwise). If its env needs box features that are off, the job first runs the box stage (a system rebuild). Job kind apps_rollback.

error.message: app generation 2 is not on disk or is the current one

apps.accept_terms.summary: Accept an installed app's vendor terms for the caller's profile (0.4). Action org.hinteros.system.apps.
apps.accept_terms.description: For apps that reached the profile without an acceptance (the starter set): id must be in the caller's env and have terms, version must be the running catalog's terms.version (invalid_params otherwise). Records {version, accepted_at, by: <user>, profile: <id>} in terms-accepted.json and the audit log; then the id leaves apps.list's needs_terms. Accepting what is already accepted is a no-op.

error.message: the current terms version of steam is 2026-09-10

profiles.list.summary: The profiles (0.4). Read-only; starts a usage scan when the data is older than an hour.
profiles.list.description: Every account of the running state.json that has metadata, with the caller (spares are not listed; first_boot: no admin profile exists). On a schema-1 box, p1 as an implicit profile after the migration created profiles.json.

locked_until.description: The PIN backoff lock (Unix seconds) while it is on.

active.description: Its session is the one on screen.

pin_set.description: false: a migrated profile without a PIN yet (show 'Set your PIN'). Always true on a schema-1 box (before the migration there are no PINs).

profiles.create.summary: Create a profile (job, a rebuild that adds the account). Action org.hinteros.system.profiles.create; also on greeter.sock.
profiles.create.description: name 1 to 32 characters (trimmed, no control or format characters; duplicates allowed), color one of ProfileColor (default teal), pin 4 to 8 digits, locked as chosen, revision = settings.get's. At 8 profiles: profile_limit. The id is taken from the counter at once (never reused, even if the job fails). On success the job writes the metadata and the PIN hash, gives the account the starter env, and (from the greeter) a one-time token so the greeter enters it without the PIN. Job kind profiles_create.

profiles.setup_admin.summary: First-boot mode: make the caller's spare account the admin profile (0.4). No job, no rebuild, no network.
profiles.setup_admin.description: Only a spare caller, only while no admin profile exists (else permission_denied {reason: profile}). Writes the metadata (admin) and the PIN hash; the account's app profile is set to the starter env right after (a short apps job when the box is idle).

profiles.rename.summary: Rename a profile (0.4). Own: no PIN; another: the admin PIN.
profiles.rename.description: pin_required {pin: admin} (with retry_after_ms during the backoff lock) when renaming another profile without the right admin PIN.

profiles.set_appearance.summary: The caller's colour and the appearance mirrored for the picker (0.4).
profiles.set_appearance.description: text_scale 0.5 to 3.0. The picker uses the most accessible combination of all profiles' values.

profiles.set_pin.summary: Change the caller's PIN (0.4). current_pin is required once a PIN is set (a migrated profile sets its first PIN without it).
profiles.set_pin.description: pin_required {pin: self} for a missing or wrong current_pin (with the backoff).

profiles.set_locked.summary: Whether the caller's profile asks for its PIN to enter (0.4). Own PIN.

profiles.reset_pin.summary: Set another profile's PIN with the admin PIN (0.4). The admin profile's own: the admin account's password (polkit org.hinteros.system.profiles.recover, interactive) instead.
profiles.reset_pin.description: For the admin profile admin_pin is not used; the service asks polkit for org.hinteros.system.profiles.recover with the session daemon's agent (authentication_required when dismissed). The target's backoff is reset.

profiles.remove.summary: Remove a profile, its home and its apps (job, a rebuild). Own PIN for yourself, the admin PIN for others; never the admin profile.
profiles.remove.description: confirm_id must equal id. The job kills every process of the account, rebuilds without it, then deletes the home (no symlink is followed, one filesystem), the PIN, the metadata, the app profile links and the registry entry. A failed or cancelled job deletes nothing. Removing your own profile: end the session first (the launcher switches to the picker). invalid_params {field: id, reason: admin} for the admin profile. Job kind profiles_remove.

error.message: the admin profile cannot be removed

profiles.switch.summary: Choose the next profile (0.4): writes the switch hint the greeter reads. A locked target needs its PIN here, before the caller's session closes anything.
profiles.switch.description: id is a profile id or guest. A locked profile (with a PIN) other than the caller's own needs pin = the target's PIN: wrong or missing is pin_required {pin: target, retry_after_ms?} and nothing is written; right, the hint carries a one-time token for the target (single use, bound to its user, valid 60 s), so the greeter enters it without any UI. The same caller may call again without pin while its token is live to extend hint and token by 60 s (a switch waiting for apps to close). The admin profile's PIN has no backoff. For the caller's own id it issues a one-time resume token (session.restart). Unlocked profiles and the guest need no PIN. The session daemon then ends the session (session.switch_profile).

examples.name: to the locked Kim, with her PIN
to the locked Kim, wrong PIN

profiles.switch_cancel.summary: Drop the caller's switch hint and its token (0.4): the switch was cancelled and the session stays.
profiles.switch_cancel.description: Only a hint the caller wrote is removed; otherwise nothing happens.

profiles.unlock.summary: The caller's PIN after sleep (0.4): the lock screen of a locked profile.
profiles.unlock.description: pin_required {pin: self, retry_after_ms?} when wrong or during the backoff lock.

guest.set.summary: Turn the guest account on or off (job, a rebuild). Admin PIN. Action org.hinteros.system.starter.
guest.set.description: job_id null when it is already so. Job kind guest_set.

guest.end.summary: End guest session (0.5): end the guest's session and wipe the guest now (job). Only the guest itself. Action org.hinteros.system.profiles.
guest.end.description: Only a caller that is the guest account (hinteros-guest, while the guest is on) may call it; anyone else gets permission_denied {reason: profile}. The service checks the account first: the name hinteros-guest, the expected guest uid (20000 on a box), no other account with that uid, a home that is an absolute path ending in /hinteros-guest; otherwise internal_error and nothing is touched. The job (kind guest_end) hides the guest from the picker (profiles-public.json guest.enabled false; PAM refuses the guest) while it runs, ends the guest's session itself (logind TerminateUser, its user slice, then SIGKILL for anything left of the uid; it fails at stage preparing if processes remain, before anything is deleted), then deletes everything the guest uid owns in its home (the home directory itself stays), in /tmp, /var/tmp and /dev/shm (top-level entries owned by the uid; no symlink is followed, no other filesystem entered, nothing owned by another uid touched), the guest's app env link (then given the starter env again), its terms acceptances (by hinteros-guest), its usage entry and a switch hint that targets it. The boot-time wipe stays. The caller's own session ends while the job runs: call it last.

error.message: only the guest can end the guest session

display.save_mode.summary: Make a display mode the box's (0.4): stored in runtime.json, published as /run/hinteros/gamescope-modes for every profile's session. Action org.hinteros.system.settings.

display.description: The display as gamescope names it in GAMESCOPE_MODE_SAVE_FILE (<make> <model>).

audio.save_output.summary: Make an audio output the box's (0.4): stored in runtime.json, published as /run/hinteros/audio-output. Action org.hinteros.system.settings.
audio.save_output.description: node is a PipeWire node name.

starter_set.get.summary: The starter set: the apps every new profile and guest session starts with (0.4). Read-only.

starter_set.set.summary: Change the starter set (job). Admin PIN; ids must be apps the admin profile has now. Action org.hinteros.system.starter.
starter_set.set.description: 0 to 16 ids, each in the admin profile's current env, else invalid_params {field: ids, reason: not_in_admin_profile}. The job builds the new starter env (an evaluation only), with the box stage when a feature is off. Only profiles and guest sessions created afterwards get it. Job kind starter_set.

jobs.get.summary: One job: running or among the last 10 finished. Read-only.

jobs.list.summary: The running job, if any, and the last 10 finished jobs, newest first. Read-only.

jobs.cancel.summary: Cancel a running job before its activation stage; the box stays unchanged. Action org.hinteros.system.jobs.cancel.

error.message: the job is activating and can no longer be cancelled

profiles_changed.summary: 0.4: profiles changed (a profile job finished, a rename, a PIN, lock or appearance change): re-query profiles.list.

job_started.summary: A job was started (by any caller).

job_progress.summary: A job reached a stage or made progress (at most 4 per second). percent only where meaningful (downloading).

job_finished.summary: A job ended. session_restart_required: the switch replaced the system service's API or the session daemon, so the launcher should offer a session restart.

error.message: the channel tip is not signed

parse_error.summary: The line is not valid JSON, not UTF-8, or longer than 64 KiB (the last two close the connection).

invalid_request.summary: Valid JSON but not a valid JSON-RPC 2.0 request (batches are not supported).

method_not_found.summary: Unknown method (or not available in the negotiated version).

invalid_params.summary: Params do not match the method's params schema (unknown fields included), or fail a semantic check. data names the field when known.

handshake_required.summary: A method other than 'hello' was called before the handshake.

version_mismatch.summary: Client and server API versions are incompatible.

already_handshaken.summary: 'hello' was called twice on one connection.

permission_denied.summary: Not allowed: the caller does not own seat0's active session (seat), polkit said no (polkit), or the peer cannot be identified safely (peer: no SO_PEERPIDFD, or the process is gone).

job_failed.summary: Only in job_finished.error and jobs.get: the job failed (or was cancelled) at stage; log_hint is the last relevant log line.

insufficient_resources.summary: Not enough memory or free disk space for a rebuild.

job_busy.summary: Another job runs (only one at a time), or the job is past the point of cancelling.

rate_limited.summary: Too many mutating requests from this user (10 per minute, burst 3).

state_conflict.summary: Stale settings revision, or update.apply's rev is not the last verified check result.

update_unreachable.summary: The update server cannot be reached (the 'home lab unreachable' screen).

update_verification_failed.summary: The channel tip is unsigned, signed by an unknown signer, or does not descend from the locked revision.

not_found.summary: Unknown generation or job; apps.install: an id that is not in the running generation's catalog; apps.remove: an id that is not installed.

needs_acknowledgement.summary: A downgrading channel or base switch without acknowledge_downgrade: true.

authentication_required.summary: polkit would allow the action only after interactive authentication (auth_admin: the admin password), and it did not happen: no authentication agent is registered for the caller (no session daemon agent, or another client than the session daemon called), or the user cancelled the prompt or did not answer in time.

app_conflict.summary: apps.install: id conflicts with conflicts_with (installed or also requested). apps.remove: conflicts_with, which stays installed, depends on id.

unavailable.summary: 0.4: the per-profile methods on a box that still has box-wide apps (state.json schema 1, before the migration job): service profiles, reason schema1.

profile_limit.summary: profiles.create with the most profiles there may be (8; the guest does not count).

pin_required.summary: A PIN is missing or wrong: the caller's own (self), the admin profile's (admin) or the profile being entered (target). retry_after_ms while the backoff lock is on (3 free failures, then 1 s doubling to 5 min, per profile).

terms_required.summary: apps.install: app id has vendor terms and accepted_terms does not name their current version (show the terms, then retry with it).

ProfileName.description: A display name: 1 to 32 characters, trimmed, no control or format characters.

BoxFeature.description: A box feature (catalog format 3): box-wide configuration an app needs, turned on when any owner has such an app.

TermsVersion.description: A vendor terms version from the catalog.

JobRef.description: A started job, or null when there was nothing to do.

rev.description: System repo revision in its config snapshot, if any.

profiles.description: The accounts in that generation's state.json with their current names (null: no longer a profile); absent if its state.json cannot be read (since 0.4). The rollback screen lists the profiles a rollback would drop or bring back empty.

readds_features.description: 0.5: box features a rollback to this generation would turn back on: the profiles' apps need them and its state.json lacks them (the rollback job re-adds them in a box stage; the rollback screen says so). Absent when there are none or it is unknown (schema 1, unreadable state.json).

security.description: Highest Security: trailer severity among the new commits; non-null means the launcher shows the full-screen security notice.

new_apps.description: Apps the update makes installable (in the target's catalog, not available in the running one), by id; null if the target's catalog could not be read (since 0.3). The Store says 'More apps are available after the next update'.

removed_apps.description: Installed apps the update takes away (removed from, or missing in, the target's catalog); null if unknown (since 0.3). The update screen names them with the reason.

version.description: (Session API 0.11; optional in system API 0.3.) The release rev carries: its release/version file if that matches ^\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ (at most 32 characters), otherwise the first 12 hex digits of rev. The launcher shows 'HinterOS <version>'. Absent from older services: show the short rev.

security_summary.description: (Session API 0.11; optional in system API 0.3.) The newest Security-Summary: trailer among the new commits: one line (control characters removed), at most 120 characters; the security notice shows it under the severity. Null if none; absent from older services.

apps_not_updated.description: 0.4: app envs the final apps stage could not rebuild; each keeps its previous generation, which still works. Absent when there were none.

owner.description: A profile id, starter or guest.

features_readded.description: 0.5 (rollback jobs): box features turned back on after the rollback, because the profiles' apps need them and the restored generation lacked them. Absent when there were none.

JobResult.description: update_check jobs: an UpdateCheckResult; jobs that change the system: an AppliedResult.

ErrorObject.description: A JSON-RPC error object (codes from this document's errors).
